findings.claim:
BLOCKING, all three tops. With the v6 tether fitted, the shade cannot be lifted, turned or lowered off by hand, and it cannot be put back.
(a) The lift jams. The snap hook hangs from the hub's eye. It sits in the 10 mm gap between the hub (r 31) and the collar's bore (r 41), standing on the lip.
- The lift has to raise the lip to z 73.5-74.5 under the PEEK ring at z 86. That leaves 12.5 mm of height at the 8.0 lift and 11.5 at the 9.0 lift.
- The drawn snap is 14 tall. A real DIN 5299 C 4 x 40 is about 19 wide (11 inside plus two 4 mm wires).
- A straight 40 mm bar in that curved gap has only about 4.8 mm of radial room. So the snap cannot lie flat and cannot tilt out of the way.
- The lift stops at about 6.5 mm with the drawn snap and about 1.5 mm with a real one. The pins need 8.0.
(b) Even if the shade could be lifted, the rope goes taut at about 21 deg of the 30 deg turn.
- Its eye holds the rigid snap's near end within 6.8 of the M4 head. So the snap's far end can reach 159.7 deg at most.
- From there the wrap round the hub to the M3 at 300 deg needs 83.5 of rope. There are 78.4.
(c) The lowering is short. Taking the whole 125.2 chain as a flexible string (so these figures are the most it can give), it goes taut after about 30 mm of lowering on the drawn counter-clockwise wrap. That wrap cannot unwind until the collar is below the carrier. The short way round, it goes taut after about 70 mm. The lane says 100.
- At about 30 mm the snap sits at the collar's top edge, inside the 10 mm gap, where no hand can unclip it.
(d) top_check.py still leaves the tether out.
Fix:
- Take the hub end of the tether out of the gap, for example to an anchor below the hub's bottom face, where the snap hangs in the open.
- Size the rope from the swept path with the snap as a rigid body, plus a hand's width.
- Add the tether to the path check.

The tether would probably not hold even once. Whatever replaces it (finding 1) must be made of parts rated for the drop.
- The rope: the lane's '2.2 kN' for 1.5 mm 7x7 is S3i's figure for 2 mm rope. 1.5 mm 7x7 316 breaks at 1.26 kN (S3i), or 1.37 kN (140 kg, GS Products).
- The snap: its maker, Elesa-Ganter, rates the 4 x 40 stainless snap at 500 N static and says not to use it for lifting. The lane's 1.9 kN is a seller's breaking figure.
- The loops: they bend round an M4 and an M3 shank (D/d 2.7 and 2.0) with no thimble, which weakens the rope further.
- A loop clamped under a button head is not a rated termination. The CAD draws no loop:
  - the 'eye' is one 6.8 mm rod from the head;
  - the M3 head sits 0.15 off the bore, with no room for a 1.5 mm loop.
- The M4 has 6 mm of thread in 6061, so pull-out is not the problem. The load is sideways. With a 1.5 mm loop under its head, the M3 bends at about 0.9-1.2 GPa at 0.8-1.1 kN, beyond A2-70's strength.
- Peak loads, redone with the rope's stretch:
  - the shade let go right after the turn (about 25 mm of free fall): 0.64-0.82 kN;
  - the bayonet giving way where the shade hangs (about 50 mm): 0.90-1.15 kN;
  - the lane's 100 mm: 1.26-1.60 kN.
  All are at or above the parts' ratings.
- Standards:
  - IEC 60598-1 asks for no shade tether. Its 4.14 'test A' adds 4 x the luminaire's weight, static (IECEE decision sheet DSH 0861).
  - The nearest published rule for a backup hanger is IEC 60598-2-17:2017, 17.7.6 (stage luminaires): it must survive a free fall of 300 mm, 30 times.
  - 'Holds once, not a margin of 10' falls short of that. The BOM row still says 'rated well over 10 x the 1.1 kg shade'.
- UL 1598 text was not opened: UNVERIFIED.

The gripper is a real part and its rating checks out, but the levelling the texts describe cannot be done with the canopy on.
- The part: Cable Grippers lists the MGR-10 MM ('MGR-M10 MM' in its chart):
  - 0.675 in (17.1) long without the plunger, a 0.47 in body, M10;
  - mounts in a 7/16 in hole, 'with safety nut'.
- The rating: the bottom-exit MGR on 1/16 in stainless 7x7 has a 312 lb minimum break and a 50 lb maximum for one cable. One later page of the catalogue prints 62 lb.
- The release is the plunger, and the knurled safety nut on it must be loosened first and tightened when level ('WHEN LEVEL TIGHTEN KNURLED NUT TO LOCK IN PLACE').
- Drawn plunger-down 1 mm above the 3 mm floor, the plunger is 4 mm up a 6 mm hole that also carries the cable.
  - No fingertip reaches it, and the safety nut cannot be turned at all.
  - So 'push each gripper's plunger from below and slide until level' cannot be done as written. The NOTES and BOM need the same correction.
- It does work with the canopy slid down the cables first (it is a separate cover on two set screws): level, lock the safety nuts, set the cord, then push the canopy up. Re-levelling means taking the canopy down.
- The maker's own system is the reverse: the gripper on the fixture, the swaged end at the canopy. Turned over in a bracket it still grips the right way, because the load pulls the cable out of the plunger end either way.
- The cable tail is drawn 13 mm above the gripper and 'cut and tucked'. Keep a longer tail. The maker asks 1 in for its looping gripper; no MGR figure was found: UNVERIFIED.

Part of the canopy's load path is not drawn, and the lock nut has no room.
- The brackets: each L bracket's vertical leg only butts against the strap's underside (51 mm2 of end contact for the two). There is no top flange, so 'riveted under the strap' cannot be done as drawn. The bracket-to-strap link carries the whole lamp.
- The nut: the drawn 16 mm round nut touches the driver's enclosure (distance 0.000).
  - A real M10 hex nut (ISO 4032, 16 across the flats) fits only with a flat against the wall.
  - A DIN 985 M10 lock nut (17 across the flats, as 'lock nut' implies) overlaps the enclosure by 23-25 mm3 in any orientation.
  - Either way there is no room for a spanner.
Fix:
- Move the grippers out to about r 43-44 (the cables still clear the floor holes), or narrow the enclosure.
- Draw the bracket's top flange and rivets, and the strap's screws to the box.
- Also: the strap is 143 long in the CAD and 138 in the BOM.

The hub end is now a part whose maker publishes it, and it needs no turning. Its rating and its seat need correcting.
- What Nicopress says:
  - 871-1-C is a copper stop sleeve for 1/16 in (1.5 mm) rope, 7/32 in (5.5) long, listed for both galvanized and stainless rope;
  - it holds 'approximately 50% of the cable's rated breaking strength'; the catalogue says stop sleeves 'typically hold to 50% of the cable's RBS'.
- On 1/16 in 7x7 302/304 (480 lb) that is about 240 lb (1.07 kN), typical, not a minimum. The 430 lb in the BOM is not on any Nicopress page I could find.
- J.R. Clancy (Wenger): 'the efficiency of these connections must be determined by testing'.
- It still gives about 127 x the 8.4 N on each cable, and about 25 x the IEC load of 4 x the weight added. So it works, if every assembly is proof-tested to a stated load. The note keeps the pull test but gives no load.
- The diameter (13/64 in) is not on Nicopress's page: UNVERIFIED.
- One Nicopress tool reference (not opened here: it returned 404) lists 871-1-C under 3/64 in cable: UNVERIFIED, to confirm with Nicopress.
- The seat: the 5.6 x 6 counterbore fits the unpressed 5.16 x 5.56 sleeve with 0.22 to spare across and 0.44 in depth.
  - Nicopress says pressing makes the sleeve longer, and the cut end must stay outside the sleeve.
  - A pressed sleeve plus its tail will very likely stand proud of the hub's face and hold the white disc off.
  - Deepen the counterbore to 8-9 (the walls allow it) and measure a pressed sample.

(a) Confirmed from the geometry at e1da219f59:
- The snap and eye sit in a closed chamber: r 31 (hub) to r 41 (bore), the lip below (r 32.5-41.1, z 64-66; crystal.py:319), the PEEK ring above (r 31-40.8 from z 86; :188).
- The slots force a lift of 8.0-9.0 from where the shade hangs. The turn passage is z 82.5-87.5 (:342) and the pins' shoulders z 91-95 (:503). So the chamber is 12.5 / 11.5 tall during the turn.
- Elesa's GN 5299-C-40 table (local PDF text) gives d2 min 11 and d3 4, so the snap is 19 wide at the big end and 14 at the eye.
- In plan view a 36-40 mm chord of 4 mm wire between r 31 and r 41 has only 0.5-1.6 mm of radial play. The snap can tilt only 1-5 deg, so it stays about 19 tall (14 as drawn).
- The lift stops at about 1.5 mm (real snap) or 6.5 (drawn). Fitting a shade ('clip the snap... push up', crystal.py:1188-1192) is blocked the same way.
(b) Confirmed:
- Entries are at 0/120/240, notches at +30 (:341-343), pins at a+30 (:503). So the collar turns +30 deg and the M3 goes from 270 to 300, lengthening the drawn counter-clockwise wrap.

- Converged, with the drawn rope and wrap: as a string it goes taut at about 88 mm (out/flex_analytic.txt).
- With the snap as a rigid 40 bar, the rope needed is 70 / 72-75 / 75.5-78 / 80-82 at 50 / 60 / 70 / 80 mm (out/chain_rigid.txt), so taut at about 70-75.

(d) Confirmed: top_check.py:14 FIXT has no tether.
The suggested fix does not work as stated. The only ways from the hub to the collar are this annulus and the 1.5 mm ring between the Ø62 disc and the Ø65 lip. A 1.5 mm rope through that ring runs line-to-line on the white paint, in view from below.
